newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreigners held 12.1 pct of Israeli shares in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners held 12.1 pct of Israeli shares in 1996.

text.p: Foreign investors held a 12.1 percent of Israeli shares traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) at the end of 1996, the Bank of Israel said on Monday citing preliminary figures.

Foreign holdings rose from 10.9 percent of total market capitalisation at the end of 1995 and 7.0 percent at the end of 1994. Foreign holdings peaked at 12.5 percent in September and October 1996, before declining slightly in the last two months of the year, the central bank said.
The central bank said most overseas holdings on the TASE were inside shareholdings, which are defined as holdings equal to five percent or more of equity.
Foreign investors accounted for 11.6 percent of inside shareholders in TASE-listed companies, unchanged from the end of 1995, the Bank of Israel said.
Foreign and local inside shareholders accounted for a preliminary 67.3 percent of the TASE's total market capitalisation at the end of 1996, up from 66.0 percent at the end of 1995.
Holdings by Israeli mutual and provident funds as a percentage of total market capitalisation declined last year.

Mutual funds held only 5.4 percent of total market capitalisation at the end of 1996, compared with 7.7 percent at the end of 1995, the Bank of Israel said. Provident funds meanwhile saw their holdings drop to 11.3 percent from 12.1 percent.
Total market capitalisation, not counting shares held by the Israeli government, rose slightly in 1996 to 98.02 billion shekels from 96.06 billion shekels a year earlier, the central bank said.
In the Israeli bond market, foreigners accounted for just 0.2 percent of market capitalisation, compared with 0.3 percent a year ago, the bank said.
